jobs.description: We are looking for a dedicated Imaging Engineer to strengthen our team! In this role you will further develop the imaging platform for our production systems but also support industrialization and R&D to turn new products and ideas into mass production. Does this sound interesting? Keep reading and welcome with your application!Who is your future team?You will join the Imaging team, a specialized group of four experienced engineers focused on developing the imaging parts needed within our production systems to produce Axis cameras with high image quality.These production systems play a critical role in supporting high-volume manufacturing operations at our global facilities, where millions of products are produced and tested annually.The Imaging team is part of a larger division of about 60+ engineers working with Production Engineering and Technology (PET), and together with our colleagues within SW, electronics and mechanical engineering we develop and maintain production systems globally.What you'll do here as Imaging EngineerAs an Imaging Engineer, you'll contribute to the design, development and maintenance of imaging production tests that enable the testing of Axis products in our production systems. You will also be a part of our development projects where we use innovative imaging and optical solutions to design efficient and reliable production systems.Typical tasks include handling topics related to optics, collimators and other imaging equipment needed to produce Axis' products.You will also play an important role in designing, developing, and maintaining software frameworks used for verification and calibration of our production systems. This includes collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless production processes.Key responsibilities include:    Designing and maintaining both SW and HW for the imaging tests framework to support production processes.    Developing and maintaining software frameworks to facilitate machine monitoring, verification, calibration and production testing using C# and Python    Providing technical support to R&D product development initiatives    Analyzing production data to drive system improvements and innovation    Contributing to strategic planning for future imaging test developmentOur team leverages a range of technologies, including:    Hardware like different types of optics and collimators    Programming languages: C#, Python, C++    Tools: Jira, Confluence, QlikView, Visual Studio, GitHub Copilot    Version control systems: Git, SVN, Gerrit    Continuous integration platforms: TeamCity    Agile methodologiesWho are we looking for/Who are you?We think you are a dedicated engineer with skills in imaging, optics and software development who is curious, responsible, organized and methodical. You enjoy problem solving and working with both hardware and software. Ability to communicate is important as the role requires collaboration with other teams and departments. The work includes a lot of freedom and independence, which requires that you are proactive and take initiative.We'd love to hear that you have:    Experience within optics, collimators or other imaging equipment    A huge interest in software development and optics    Finding solutions to complex technical problems    Interest in the complexity of production and creating efficient production systems for our factories around the world    University degree preferably within computer science, engineering, physics, electrical engineering or equivalent    At least a couple of years of experience from roles in a development organization    Good communication skills in English and Swedish, both in speech and writingThe position is full time. Travelling is not required, but there will probably be possibilities to visit our factories around the world.What Axis has to offerWe are a world leader in network video, where cutting-edge technology meets global impact. Here, you'll contribute to meaningful projects that shape the future of security and surveillance - developing solutions used worldwide.As a fast-growing company, we offer exciting career opportunities. You'll grow professionally through continuous learning, supported by a collaborative team that values creativity, innovation, and work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us. We offer a range of benefits, including a company bonus, Friday cake, wellness allowance, health insurance - and even your own Axis bicycle.To learn more about Axis, our innovative products, solutions, and vibrant company culture, explore:Life at Axis blogEngineering at Axis blogInnovation at AxisReady to Act?Axis is a company realizing the benefits of a diverse workforce. We know that diversity in groups creates a better working environment and promotes creativity, something that is fundamental for our success. We welcome all applications. We go through applications continuously so don't wait - send in your application today!In case of questions, please reach out to recruiting manager Michael Rosenberg at +46 46 272 1800

jobs.occupation: Associate researcher in Experimental lung transplantation
jobs.description: Description of workplaceThe research group is led by Associated professor Sandra Lindstedt and has a long-standing interest in research related to lung transplantation, post-transplant complications, and lung regeneration. The group focuses on developing novel therapeutic strategies to treat lung injury, improve donor organ quality, and reduce complications following lung transplantation. A particular focus is on acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and regenerative approaches to lung repair.We offerLund University is a governmental authority, which means you get special benefits, generous holidays, and a favorable occupational pension. Read more on the university's website about being employed at Lund University, Work at Lund UniversityWork descriptionA associate researcher position is available within the Lindstedt research group, focusing on translational research in lung transplantation, lung injury, and regenerative medicine. The duties at the research unit primarily consist of experimental and laboratory-based research, with a particular focus on the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies to improve lung repair and transplantation outcomes.The main responsibilities include:    independently designing, planning, coordinating, and conducting research projects, as well as collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and managing experimental data.    The work involves the development and optimization of experimental protocols, evaluation of therapeutic interventions, and application of cellular, molecular, ultra-high-plexed immunofluorescence and histological techniques to investigate mechanisms of lung injury, repair, and regeneration.    The position also includes responsibility for preparing high-quality scientific manuscripts for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, contributing to research grant applications, and presenting research findings at national and international scientific conferences.    The majority of the work will be conducted independently, while also involving close collaboration with internal and external research partners and clinical collaborators.    In addition, the position includes mentorship and supervision of doctoral students, Bachelor’s and Master’s students, and other junior researchers, as well as contributing to the coordination and development of ongoing research activities within the group.Other work tasks might also be included.QualificationsRequired qualifications    PhD (or equivalent) in biomedical sciences, biotechnology, molecular biology, regenerative medicine, or a related field.    A minimum of four years of documented research experience following completion of the PhD, demonstrating scientific independence and responsibility.    Documented experience in experimental and translational biomedical research, particularly within cell therapies, lung injury, lung transplantation, or regenerative medicine.    Hands-on experience with small and large-animal models and/or ex vivo organ perfusion.    Experience with standard cellular and molecular biology techniques, including cell culture, ELISA, Western blotting, qPCR, immunohistochemistry and high-plexed immunofluorescence.    Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, coordinate, and conduct complex experimental research projects.    Documented scientific productivity through publications in international peer-reviewed journals.    Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.    Independent and responsible, with the ability to organize and manage research activities and take responsibility for scientific quality and project progress.    Collaborative, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary research environments.    Analytical and solution-oriented, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and address complex scientific challenges.Meritorious qualifications:    Additional specialized training in experimental transplantation, regenerative medicine, cell therapy, or related disciplines.    Relevant training and certification in laboratory animal science, particularly involving large- and small-animal experimental models.    Completed courses in higher education teaching and pedagogy.    Experience with experimental lung transplantation, including large- and small-animal models of lung injury and transplantation.    Hands-on experience with ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) and human ex vivo lung models, including precision-cut lung slices (PCLS).    Experience in the development and evaluation of cell-based and regenerative therapies, particularly mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and mitochondrial therapeutics.    Experience with cellular, molecular, histological, and proteomic analyses, including the handling and processing of human and animal tissue samples.    Experience in managing and coordinating interdisciplinary research projects and national or international collaborations.    Documented experience in scientific supervision, preparation of research grant applications, and dissemination of research findings through publications and international conferences.Other informationThe position is a fixed-term employment according to the Special Fixed-term Employment (SÄVA) regulations §5 p1 LAS, and it is full-time. The desired start date is 2027-01-01 or as agreed upon, with an end date of 2027-12-31.How to ApplyApplications are to be submitted via the University’s recruitment system. The application should include a CV and a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a degree certificate or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.).

Department of Biosystems and TechnologyPhD Project: Valorization and Risk Assessment of Anaerobic Digestates for Sustainable Horticultural ProductionThird-cycle subject area: Horticultural ScienceDescription of the doctoral project The transition to circular food and energy systems requires safe, high-quality products that can return nutrients and organic matter to horticultural production. Anaerobic digestate from biogas production is a promising resource containing plant nutrients and organic fibre originating from, for example, manure, food and household waste, slaughterhouse by-products, park and garden residues, and biomass from intermediate crops or roadside vegetation. The digestate can be separated into a nutrient-rich liquid fraction and a fibre fraction. While the liquid fraction has potential for use in nutrient solutions, the fibre fraction is particularly relevant as a constituent of growing media and a potential partial replacement for peat and other fibre materials. Developing safe, functional and locally available alternatives to peat is an important challenge for sustainable horticultural production. A key barrier is the possible presence of pyralid herbicide residues. These herbicides can accumulate in crop material, persist during anaerobic digestion and cause growth disturbances in sensitive horticultural crops at very low concentrations. The project will investigate the occurrence and fate of pyralids in selected feedstocks and digestate fractions, with particular focus on the fibre fraction and its use in growing media.About the positionThe doctoral project will combine greenhouse and growth-chamber bioassays with laboratory studies and chemical characterisation. It will assess effects on plant growth and nutrient uptake, examine the distribution, degradation and immobilisation of herbicide residues, and generate knowledge to support risk assessment and the safe valorisation of digestate-derived growing-media products. The project is an important part in the ongoing transition for more circular productions systems where plant nutrients and fiber is recycled from waste to production. The project is a part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center, which means that there will be collaboration with other PhD students both at SLU and at Linköping University. Communication of results, both orally and in writing to both academic and industrial stakeholders are also important parts of the project. As a PhD-student, you will also take PhD courses and be a part of the daily work at the department.RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in Horticultural Science. To meet the specific entry requirements the applicant must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.You should have received a degree at advanced level (second cycle) within the fields of Horticultural Science, Agricultural Science, or similar subject. You should also have documented experience with laboratory work and experimental work within the field of study.Beneficial competences Driver’s licence valid in Sweden. Documented experience from scientific writing and scientific communication.Your profileWe are looking for an engaged and self-going candidate with genuine interest in horticulture and circular solutions. Suitable backgrounds are as a Horticulturist or Agronomist. Experience with laboratory work, for example microbial analyses, is beneficial. You should also have experience with practical plant cultivation. Great emphasis will be put on personal skills like curiosity, ability to work individually and in group, and ability to independently plan and perform research related tasks. You are expected to be open to new challenges and to take on various work tasks to contribute to the development of the department’s activities. Very good skills in speaking and writing in English is mandatory.About usAt the department of Biosystems and Technology you will work in a multi-disciplinary environment together with around 60 colleagues, among which around 10 PhD students. The holder of this position will be a part of a national, transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities (Linköping University and SLU) and about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system and has additional support from Swedish Energy Agency. All doctoral positions advertised within BSRC will be formulated so that they fit into the competence center's research plans and at the same time reflect our parties' interests. This way, we ensure long-term competence supply to both industry and academia.Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/Form of employment / Funding Employment as a doctoral student (4-year programme). Location: Alnarp, SwedenScope: 100%Start date: Upon agreement, but preferably 2027-01-01.Application and selection: Please submit your application using the link below. The deadline is November 27, 2026. Applications cannot be submitted through the recruitment system on 20–22 November due to a system update.Read more about the attachments that your application should include at https://www.slu.se/en/study/programmes-courses/doctoral-education/how-can-i-become-a-doctoral-student/application/Selection among eligible applicants is based on the documents attached to the application, and is carried out with regard to the applicant’s ability to complete the programme within the allotted time.

jobs.occupation: PhD student in biomass resources from sustainable cropping systems
jobs.description: Department of Biosystems and Technology PhD project in Agricultural Science: Using agricultural crop biomass for biogas in synergy with the development of sustainable cropping systems Note: This advertisement is abbreviated to fit in Platsbanken's recruitment tool. To view the ad in its entirety including additional information, please visit https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/jobs-and-vacancies/ About the positionTargeting the sustainable supply of agricultural crop biomass as substrates for biogas, the project will use a field experiment platform to investigate crop yields and crop nutrient dynamics in different scenarios for biomass removal and nutrient redistribution via digestates. The research will primarily be based on an ongoing long-term cropping systems experiment with four distinct systems: conventional, organic, agroforestry and perennial cereal.The biomass resources to be studied include, but are not limited to: cover crops, ley, straw (from cereals, grain legumes and oilseed crops), beet leaves, and possibly wood. Studies on quantities and nutrient contents of different biomasses build on existing data from the experiment, to be complemented with additional sample collection and analyses as well as literature data or data from agricultural statistics databases. The holder of this position will be a part of a national transdisciplinary center of excellence called Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC). Here, co-production of new and relevant knowledge is generated through collaboration between different scientific disciplines as well as between researchers and practitioners from industry and public organizations. The BSRC includes researchers and support from two universities, Linköping University and Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, as well as about 50 private and public organizations involving all parts of the biogas system. It also has support from the Swedish Energy Agency. All doctoral positions advertised within BSRC will be formulated so that they fit into the competence center's research plans and at the same time reflect our parties' interests. This way, we ensure long-term competence supply to both industry and academia. RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39). You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6. You should have a Master’s degree, or equivalent qualification, in a relevant field such as agricultural engineering (with specialization in crop production), agricultural science, agroecology, agronomy, biology, environmental science, horticultural science or another closely related discipline. Your profileWe are looking for a highly motivated candidate with an interest in sustainable agriculture and bioeconomy systems, and in analysing complex interactions between biomass and food production and cropping system sustainability. Experience or documented knowledge in one or several of the following areas is particularly relevant:    agricultural cropping systems, crop management and diversification;    systems analysis and/or multi-criteria sustainability assessments;    modelling or scenario analysis;    bioenergy systems based on agricultural crop biomass resources;    nutrient cycling e.g. via redistribution of biomass resources and biogas digestates;    crop and soil nutrient dynamics and nutrient balances at field and cropping system levels;    statistical analysis and handling of datasets with multiple experimental factors and response variables The project strives to provide knowledge for several societal sectors (bioenergy, food production, environmental impact), it is therefore important to have an ability to understand and integrate information from different scientific fields. The successful candidate should have good analytical skills, be able to work independently and systematically, and at the same time enjoy collaboration in an interdisciplinary research environment. Excellent written and spoken English is required. Good communication skills and an interest in communicating research both scientifically and to stakeholders are important. Knowledge of Swedish is advantageous but not a requirement. Personal qualities, motivation for doctoral studies and the ability to successfully complete the research project will be given considerable weight in the selection process. jobs.occupation: PhD student in agricultural bioeconomy systems
jobs.description: Department of Biosystems and TechnologyPhD project: Sustainable utilisation of agricultural green biomass in integrated protein and biogas systemsSubject area: TechnologyDescription of the doctoral project A circular and fossil-independent bioeconomy requires renewable biomass without increasing competition for agricultural land and food production. Crop residues and intermediate crops are therefore particularly relevant resources. Research at SLU shows that these biomass resources can be substantial, but their potential and sustainable utilisation vary regionally. They can be used for biogas, while effects on soil carbon and nutrient cycling need to be considered.  Green biomass can also be biorefined into plant protein for feed or food, after which the remaining streams are used for biogas. The same feedstock can thereby provide protein, energy and recycled nutrients.The project aims to assess the potential and consequences of large-scale utilisation of green crop residues and intermediate crops in integrated biogas and green biorefinery systems.The project will:    assess sustainably available biomass from green crop residues and intermediate crops in Sweden;    assess the potential for biogas and combined plant protein and biogas production;    develop implementation scenarios based on feedstock availability, infrastructure, logistics and markets;    assess effects on nutrient cycling, soil carbon, biomethane, fertilizer use, and feed and food production; and    evaluate economic and wider socio-economic benefits, drawbacks and trade-offs.The project combines GIS and agricultural data with mass and nutrient balances, scenario modelling, and life cycle-based, techno-economic and socio-economic methods. Data will be drawn from research, statistics, literature and national databases.The doctoral student will join an interdisciplinary research environment at SLU Alnarp focusing on sustainable agricultural production, bioenergy, circular bioeconomy and systems analysis.About the positionThe work includes collection and processing of agricultural and process data, GIS, modelling of biomass and product flows, scenario development, and environmental and economic assessments.  You will integrate information from crop production and biomass availability to biorefineries, biogas, and food and energy systems.  You will analyse data, develop models and scenarios, and publish and present research results. The work will be conducted with researchers at SLU and external partners.  The doctoral student will be part of the Biogas Solutions Research Center (BSRC), a national transdisciplinary centre where Linköping University, SLU and around 50 private and public organisations collaborate. The centre is supported by the Swedish Energy Agency. The PhD project follows BSRC’s research plans and contributes to long-term competence development in industry and academia.RequirementsTo meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in technology. To meet the specific entry requirements, you must have the equivalent knowledge to a minimum of 90 credits in relevant subject areas. This must include a degree project, and at least 30 credits must be at the advanced level.  You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.You should have a Master’s degree or equivalent in, for example, biosystems/agricultural engineering, environmental engineering, agricultural science, energy systems, industrial ecology, environmental science or a related field.Your profileWe are looking for a motivated candidate interested in sustainable agricultural and bioeconomy systems and quantitative analysis.Experience or documented knowledge in one or several of the following areas is desirable:    systems analysis, modelling or scenario analysis;    GIS and spatial analysis;    life cycle assessment, environmental systems analysis or material-flow analysis;    techno-economic or socio-economic assessment;    bioenergy, biogas or biorefinery systems;    agricultural production systems and agricultural biomass;    statistical analysis and handling of larger datasets;    experience of programming or quantitative modelling, for example using Python, R or MATLAB.You should have good analytical skills, be able to integrate information from different fields, work independently and collaborate well.Excellent written and spoken English is required. Good communication skills are important. Knowledge of Swedish is advantageous but not required.Personal qualities, motivation and the ability to successfully complete doctoral studies will be given considerable weight. About usThe Department of Biosystems and Technology develops knowledge for sustainable and resource-efficient agriculture, horticulture and bioeconomy through research combining biological production systems, technology and systems analysis. The project lies at the intersection of agriculture, biosystems engineering, sustainability assessment and bioeconomy. jobs.occupation: Mechanical Engineer  From CAD Clean-up to Next-Generation Boat Design
jobs.description: Mechanical Engineer“Make X Shore’s CAD data something production can build from without guessing. Audit and rebuild assemblies, align them with the factory floor, and then help design the next-generation boat.”About the RoleX Shore’s existing CAD models and assemblies don’t fully reflect what’s actually being built on the factory floor — data has drifted from production reality, making it hard to trust drawings, plan rework, or hand off clean information to manufacturing. We’re looking for a Mechanical Engineer to audit and rebuild that CAD data, get it aligned with how boats are actually produced, and then move on to design work on X Shore’s next-generation boat platform.This is a hands-on role in two phases. First, you’ll dig into existing CAD, correct what’s out of sync with production, and work closely with the shop floor to close the gap between design intent and built reality. Once that foundation is solid, you’ll shift into forward-looking platform design for future boats. You’ll report to the Mechanical Engineering & Analysis Manager and be based on-site in Nyköping.Key Responsibilities    Audit existing CAD models and assemblies for accuracy, completeness, and structure    Rebuild or correct CAD data that no longer reflects what’s actually being built in production    Align CAD assemblies and drawings with current production reality, working directly with the shop floor    Identify and resolve discrepancies between design intent and manufactured parts    Maintain clean, well-structured CAD/PDM practices going forward    Support production with drawings, tolerances, and design clarifications during rework and manufacturing    Once alignment work is complete, contribute to the design and detailing of X Shore’s next-generation boat platform    Collaborate with electrical, production, and manufacturing engineering teams to ensure designs are manufacturableRequired Qualifications    Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent practical experience    3-5+ years of experience in mechanical design, ideally in a manufacturing environment    Expert-level SOLIDWORKS proficiency — this is a must-have, including assemblies, drawings, and PDM    Demonstrated experience auditing, cleaning up, or rebuilding CAD data and assemblies    Comfortable working directly with production to resolve build discrepancies    Fluent in English; Swedish is a plus    Ability to work on-site in NyköpingDesirable Qualifications    Experience with composites and/or metals typical of marine or automotive manufacturing    Background in boat building, automotive, or another complex hardware environment    Familiarity with GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis    Experience contributing to a new product platform from early concept through releasePersonal QualitiesDetail-oriented and methodical, comfortable untangling messy legacy data without losing momentum. Equally at home on the shop floor verifying fit as at a CAD workstation. Takes ownership, follows through, and communicates clearly across engineering and production.Success Metrics (First 12 Months)    CAD data and assemblies for existing boats are audited, corrected, and aligned with what’s built in production    Production has accurate, trustworthy drawings and models to work from    Discrepancies between design and manufactured parts are identified and resolved    Meaningful contribution made to next-generation boat platform designLocation & StructureOn-site at X Shore Factory & HQ, Nyköping. Reports to the Mechanical Engineering & Analysis Manager.

We have the power of over 50,000 students and co-workers. Students who provide hope for the future. Co-workers who contribute to Linköping University meeting challenges of today. Our fundamental values rest on credibility, trust and security. By having the courage to think freely and innovate, our actions together, large and small, contribute to a better world. We look forward to receiving your application! Are you interested in the potential of citizens' assemblies and other democratic innovations to drive climate transformation? Come join us!Work assignments The Environmental Change division (tema Miljöförändring) at the Department of Thematic Studies is looking to hire a two-year postdoctoral researcher specializing in democratic innovations.You will be part of the Formas-funded research project Democratic Innovations for Climate Transformation (2027-2029), which entails a systematic and interdisciplinary knowledge synthesis of how climate citizens’ assemblies and related democratic processes can contribute to system transformation. The project explores what the existing research literature tells us about the political impact of climate assemblies, how they might contribute to broader systemic transformations, and what this means for Swedish climate governance.As postdoc on the project, you will take a leading role in carrying out the systematic literature review across academic databases and grey literature, following established standards for searching, screening, and quality assessment. You will contribute centrally to the comparative synthesis of findings across studies, and to identifying evidence gaps in how deliberative processes connect to system-level transformation. You will also help design and facilitate stakeholder dialogues with Swedish municipalities and practitioners, which ensures that the resulting knowledge is robust and genuinely useful for policy and practice.You will work in close collaboration with the project’s principal investigator and a research team from LiU and Stockholm Resilience Centre. There is considerable room to help shape the project’s methodological choices and analytical framework, and to co-author academic outputs arising from the review and synthesis work.As postdoc, you will principally carry out research. A certain amount of teaching may be part of your duties, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.QualificationsTo be qualified to take employment as postdoc, you must have been awarded a doctoral degree or have a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree. This degree must have been awarded at the latest by the point at which LiU makes its decision to employ you.Your doctoral degree should preferably have been awarded no more than three years ago. If there are special reasons, a degree awarded more than three years ago may be accepted. Special reasons include sick leave, parental leave, trade union positions of trust, service in the defense, or other similar circumstances, as well as service or assignments relevant to the subject area.We are looking for someone with a doctoral degree in social sciences, humanities, or related fields, and a demonstrated familiarity with the research area of democratic innovations – for example, deliberative democracy, citizens’ assemblies, participatory governance, or environmental/climate governance. Experience carrying out systematic literature reviews and others forms of qualitative content analysis is considered a merit. So is prior experience with stakeholder involvement and co-production through workshops and similar formats.You are curious, rigorous, and comfortable moving between the fine-grained work of systematic screening and coding and the bigger-picture task of synthesizing what it all means. You enjoy working collaboratively, taking initiative, and are able to communicate complex research to non-academic audiences, such as policymakers and practitioners. A strong command of written and spoken English is required.The workplaceYou will be employed at the Department of Thematic Studies where you will be affiliated with the Environmental Change theme. You can read about the workplace https://liu.se/en/organisation/liu/tema/temam.The employmentThis employment is a temporary full-time contract of two years. Starting date is Januari 1, 2027, or as soon as possible. Salary and employment benefitsAt Linköping University, salaries are set individually and differentiated, in accordance with the applicable collective agreements (RALS/RALS-T) and the university’s salary-setting guidelines.More information about employee benefits is available https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/employee-benefits.Union representativesInformation about union representatives, see https://liu.se/en/work-at-liu/hjalp%20for%20sokande.Application procedureApply for the position by clicking the “Apply” button. Your application must be received no later than 27 November, 2026.Applications and documents received after the date above will not be considered. Please attach your selected research publications electronically, in pdf or word format, in the application template. Research publications, e.g. monographs, which cannot be sent electronically should be sent in three sets by mail to the University Registrar at Linköping University, University Registrar, S-581 83 Linköping, Sweden. The publications must be received by Linköping University no later than the deadline for application. Please note that printed publications will not be returned. They will be archived at Linköping University. In the event of a discrepancy between the English translation of the job announcement and the Swedish original, the Swedish version shall take precedent. We welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives - diversity enriches our work and helps us grow. Preserving everybody's equal value, rights and opportunities is a natural part of who we are. Read more about our work with: https://liu.se/en/article/lika-villkor/.We look forward to receiving your application! Linköping university has framework agreements and wishes to decline direct contacts from staffing- and recruitment companies as well as vendors of job advertisements.

jobs.occupation: Technical Procurement Manager– Utility-scale solar and BESS
jobs.description: Do you want to lead procurement for the construction of the largest solar and battery storage projects in the Nordics? We are looking for a skilled procurement professional with a strong commercial foundation and the curiosity to understand technical solutions in depth. You are willing to dig into specifications, ask questions and work closely with engineers and suppliers to make well-informed purchasing decisions in a rapidly evolving industry. Join us and be part of an ambitious team building the energy infrastructure of tomorrow.What will you do at NYAB? As our Technical Procurement Manager, you will work at the intersection of long-term sourcing strategy and practical project delivery, leading procurement for utility-scale solar and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects. Your scope will include core components and services such as solar modules, inverters, mounting systems, transformers, batteries, subcontractors and related technical solutions. In this role, you will:     Own and develop the end-to-end procurement lifecycle, from early tendering and supplier evaluation to contracting and execution.     Lead strategic and commercial negotiations to secure competitive terms, balanced risk positions and strong contractual outcomes.     Evaluate supplier offers against technical requirements, cost, quality and delivery needs, working with engineering colleagues to clarify specifications and understand trade-offs.    Stay ahead of the market by identifying new technologies, suppliers and system solutions that strengthen our renewable energy projects and make our supply chain more resilient    Drive procurement priorities against project requirements, schedules and budgets – and make sure we deliver. You will act as our internal product owner, digging into specifications, drawings and technical documentation together with the engineering team until you know the product as well as the supplier does. About you You are a goal-oriented self-starter with the persistence to follow through and make things happen. You combine sound commercial judgment with technical curiosity and a willingness to work through details, ask questions and understand what you are buying. You remain composed during complex contractual discussions and take ownership of your commitments, combining speed with precision and going the extra mile when it matters. Along the way, you build trust with colleagues, suppliers and partners.We believe you have:     A master’s degree in engineering, preferably within electrical engineering, mechanical engineering or energy systems.     At least three years of hands-on experience in large-scale procurement projects with complex technical scopes, ideally in an EPC environment.     Experience in end-to-end sourcing, supplier management and commercial or contractual negotiations.     Strong cost awareness and the ability to manage priorities within time and budget constraints.     Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.     The willingness to travel internationally to meet suppliers and partners, and to visit project sites in Sweden and abroad. It is an advantage if you have:     Experience in construction, electrical systems, renewable energy or another technically complex project environment.     Experience procuring equipment or services for solar parks, BESS or related energy infrastructure.     Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Swedish.Why work at NYAB? NYAB's greatest strength is our drive and the pride we take in our work. We all pull in the same direction – forward. We value people for their competence and initiative, and you get the freedom to act along with the accountability that comes with it. Our entrepreneurial spirit is built on collaboration and commitment. We are a close-knit community where colleagues support one another, share knowledge and work together to find solutions when new challenges arise. You will never work alone – you will have the support of colleagues and leaders, and plenty of room to grow. We also offer:    Comprehensive health assessments     Generous wellness allowance     Parental pay supplement    Reduced working hours – (Sw: arbetstidsförkortning)    A secure pension planReady to make it happen? Apply with your CV or LinkedIn profile. We review applications on an ongoing basis and look forward to hearing from you. Start: As agreed   Employment type: Full-time   Location: Hägersten, Stockholm

In addition, we provide local benefits, modern tools, and flexible ways of working that support a healthy work-life balance.Want to know more? Please note that we do not accept applications via e-mail.  We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, please submit your application before November 27th. For positions with people leadership responsibilities in Sweden, delegated Health, Safety & Environmental (HSE) responsibilities form an integral part of the role. We work together with our customers throughout the entire lifecycle, delivering cutting-edge technologies and services as well as mission-critical automation and flow control solutions. Backed by more than 225 years of industrial experience and a global team of over 19,000 professionals close to customers, we are uniquely positioned to transform industries toward a regenerative tomorrow. At Valmet, diversity of thought drives innovation. We are committed to a respectful and inclusive environment, where people can be themselves and are supported to contribute at their best.

jobs.employer_name: Who Collaborating Centre For Int Drug Monitoring
jobs.description: Would you like to contribute to safer use of medicines and vaccines globally? We are looking for a Data Scientist for the Research Department at Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC). You will join a multicultural and dynamic environment with a clear focus to ensure patient safety globally.Since 1978, Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) has been dedicated to developing, supporting, and expanding the field of pharmacovigilance science and practice.As a World Health Organization (WHO) Collaborating Centre, we support work around the world to examine the potential adverse effects of medicines and vaccines and contribute to safer, more informed care of patients.We are a diverse, international group of pharmacists, physicians, data scientists, system developers, communicators, and many other professionals motivated by a deep belief that the work we do matters.About the roleResearch at UMC is a team effort. Pharmacovigilance experts, engineers, and data scientists work side by side to develop the best ideas and solutions. We are looking for a Data Scientist with excellent technical skills who thrives on collaboration. You will join a self-organising agile team where members share ideas openly, plan their work together, give each other honest feedback, and take joint ownership of outcomes.You will report to our Head of Data Science, Angnis Schmidt-May.What you will do You will help us make better use of data from different sources, the main one being our global database of adverse event reports. Your work will mostly cover the following areas:    Machine learning, natural language processing & large language models: develop methods to support signal management using data from case reports and scientific literature. You will judge carefully when and how AI can be trusted to enhance our research.    Scientific research and dissemination: design and run studies in internal and external collaborations, publish in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences.    Sharing methods and assets: make our methods and tools available to others, for example as open-source packages, documented workflows, and reusable models.    Product research: develop innovative methods and conduct exploratory research to improve UMC's products and services. You will work closely with product teams to turn research ideas into useful product features.Who you are    You are an excellent collaborator. You listen to others and build on their ideas. We are looking for a researcher in Psychology for a fixed-term position at the School of Behavioral, Social and Legal Sciences (BSR). The research is within the area of cognitive neuroscience of aging.Subject areaThe subject area for this position is Psychology.BackgroundThe Division of Psychology at Örebro University is part of the School of Behavioural, Social and Legal Sciences (BSR), together with the Divisions of Legal Science, Criminology, and Social Work.Örebro university is now hiring a researcher within the area of cognitive neuroscience of aging, with a particular focus on early life predictors of brain structural and functional connectivity in older age. The research will be conducted within the research environment LEADER (Center for Lifespan Developmental Research), which is headed by Jonas Persson, Professor in Psychology.Duties and responsibilitiesThe research duties include preprocessing and analyses of structural and functional brain imaging data obtained by magnetic resonance imaging. A particular focus will be on analysing diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) data to assess structural connectivity and brain network properties in older age and how these related to health, cognition, lifestyle and other factors in childhood and adolescence. Analyses of functional connectivity data from resting-state fMRI images and the relationship with early life predictors is also expected. The applicant will also have a leading role in dissemination of the results through international peer-reviewed publication and presentations.
